_what: What counts as new for the person on each screen, and what the New for you strip on Home shows. Owned by src/new-work.mjs. A count row names a sidebar screen (`surface`, an id in src/workspace/surfaces.json) and where its count comes from: `source` `activity` (the default) counts the rows of the person's AI activity record (src/activity-marks.json) whose `tools` it lists (or every tool, with `tools` "every"), made by an AI (never what the person did on their own page), after the person last saw that screen; `where` narrows by a fact the row keeps (`fact` and `starts_with`, any of them). `source` `space_unread` is the unread count of every space the person is in, which opening each space clears. A screen the person has never opened counts only the last `window_days` days, and so does one last seen longer ago. The window's start moves in steps of `window_step_minutes`, so a count may hold a row up to one step older than `window_days`. The strip lists the newest rows made by an AI whose tool is in `strip.tools`, at most `strip.count`, each marked new when it came after the person last saw `strip.surface`, the same thing once (its newest row), and `looks` says how something that is not a file shows (an icon and the words for its kind); a file shows its own picture (src/workspace/file-previews.json). A new kind of made thing is a row here and a mark in activity-marks.json; no code changes. `badge_kind` says what a screen's count is, for how its sidebar row shows it (parts/sidebar/read-data/sidebar-badge-marks.json): the top-level value for every row, a row's own for that row; `notification` for unread notifications (a space's unread messages), which a collapsed sidebar shows as a red dot. `reconcile_after_ms` is how long a burst of removals waits before the store's own count is read to settle a row's badge (src/workspace/badge-counts.ts). `badge_events` names the row a real write moves at once, before the store's count settles it: the person marking a space seen takes its unread off `space_seen.removes_from`; an AI's activity record changing adds one to `ai_activity.adds_to`. A typed `badge` frame from the store (src/live-screen.mjs badge) names an event in this list and an amount; another member withdrawing an item this person had not seen takes it off `space_item_withdrawn.removes_from`. A new event is a row here and a writer that sends it.
